note.text: A drainage basin is the area contributing water to a river system; a divide separates neighbouring basins. Cameroon’s rivers connect to several larger drainage systems. The Sanaga and coastal rivers such as the Nyong reach the Atlantic. The Benue feeds the Niger system; the Dja and Sangha connect towards the Congo; the Logone and Chari connect to Lake Chad. Some school classifications separate the Sanaga from other coastal basins. Use the convention requested while preserving the correct downstream connections.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to trace major river-basin connections and explain the role of divides rather than assuming all rivers share one outlet. Builds on: Cameroon’s relief and the meaning of slope. Leads to: climate, vegetation and water-related land-use questions.

The Sanaga and coastal rivers such as the Nyong reach the Atlantic. The Benue feeds the Niger system; the Dja and Sangha connect towards the Congo; the Logone and Chari connect to Lake Chad. Some school classifications separate the Sanaga from other coastal basins. Use the convention requested while preserving the correct downstream connections.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: The schematic shows connections, not measured river courses, borders or distances. Trace each arrow downstream. A tributary joins a larger river; it does not necessarily reach the sea independently. The Lake Chad basin has no normal river outlet to the ocean, unlike the Niger and Congo systems. Relief helps establish flow directions and divides, while rainfall, storage and human use affect seasonal discharge.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Distinguish the direction of a diagram arrow from compass direction on a map. Explain one use such as water supply, irrigation, fishing or hydropower alongside a constraint such as seasonality, sediment, falls or flooding. A drawn line does not prove year-round navigability or safe drinking water. Use supplied information rather than entering a river channel.

right.text: drainage basin: the land area contributing water towards a river system.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: A basin includes contributing land and tributaries, not just the channel. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.text: divide: a boundary separating adjacent drainage basins.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: A divide separates drainage, whereas a confluence joins channels. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.text: tributary connection: a smaller river joining a larger downstream system.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: Trace its confluence and downstream river rather than assuming a separate ocean mouth. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.text: internal drainage: drainage into a basin without a normal river outlet to the ocean.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: The Lake Chad basin is internally drained, unlike the direct Atlantic-draining example. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.
